note: A curated, ordered judgement about which OpenRouter free-tier models suit this workspace's tool-calling and strict-JSON planning workload, with no benchmark number cited or invented. It is not a skill measurement and not a claim that any id is available: availability is measured only by "python3 scripts/models.py --probe-free", whose observation is recorded in the availability block below. A paid id is refused with a reason and never routed. The order is a starting point; the refusal rules and the probe are what the workspace acts on.
ranking_basis: Free-tier ids only. Ordered by capability class for a tool-calling / strict-JSON planning workload: general model class and instruction-following reliability of the family, whether the publisher declares response_format / structured_outputs support (this client sends a strict json_schema with provider.require_parameters, so an id without that declaration cannot serve the workload at all), context window, and the risk of an experimental or preview generation. Every placement is a judgement and says so in its own reason; no score, confidence or benchmark value is attached.
membership_evidence: All seven ranked ids, and the thirteen published free ids that are deliberately not ranked, were observed by this workspace itself in an OpenRouter catalogue read through scripts/models.py --probe-free, whose result is recorded in the availability block of this file.

models.why: 120B-class sparse mixture-of-experts general model, published with tool calling and structured output, 262k context. Placed first on model class and published schema support, which is a judgement about fit for a strict-JSON planning turn rather than a benchmark. Membership and response_format support are both observed in the workspace's own catalogue read recorded in the availability block (scripts/models.py --probe-free).

The pro tier of the nex-n2.5 family, 262k context, published with tool calling and structured output. Placed second behind the larger model on class alone, which is a judgement with no benchmark behind it. Membership and response_format support are both observed in the workspace's own catalogue read recorded in the availability block (scripts/models.py --probe-free).

Dense 31B instruction model, 262k context, published with tool calling and structured output. Ranked below the two larger models as a judgement about compound-plan reliability, and above the smaller ids on the same judgement. Membership and response_format support are both observed in the workspace's own catalogue read recorded in the availability block (scripts/models.py --probe-free).

Long-context 512k model published with structured output. It is a preview id the publisher can retire without notice, so durability is a judgement that places it after the stable ids even though its window is the largest ranked here. Membership and response_format support are both observed in the workspace's own catalogue read recorded in the availability block (scripts/models.py --probe-free).

The smaller sibling of the ranked nex-n2.5 pro id: same 262k context and schema support, expected to be faster and less reliable on decomposed plans, which is an expectation and not a measurement. Membership and response_format support are both observed in the workspace's own catalogue read recorded in the availability block (scripts/models.py --probe-free).

Sparse 26B variant of the gemma-4 line with the same published schema support and window, ranked below the dense 31B on a judgement about instruction adherence in multi-task plans. Membership and response_format support are both observed in the workspace's own catalogue read recorded in the availability block (scripts/models.py --probe-free).

2.6B model with a 65k window and published structured output: kept last as the single-simple-task fallback, which is a judgement about capacity rather than a measurement. Membership and response_format support are both observed in the workspace's own catalogue read recorded in the availability block (scripts/models.py --probe-free).

not_routable_by_this_client.reason: The client requests a strict json_schema response_format with provider.require_parameters, so an id whose catalogue entry does not declare response_format support is never placed in the routing order.
